title: maxk
summary: Return the k largest elements in MATLAB and RunMat.

gpu_support.notes: Device-resident tensors are gathered to the host because RunMat Accelerate does not expose top-k provider hooks yet.

description: `maxk(A,k)` returns the largest `k` values from each slice of `A` along the first non-singleton dimension. A second output returns one-based indices within the selected dimension.
behaviors: `maxk(A,k)` selects along the first non-singleton dimension and clamps nonnegative `k` to that dimension's length. `k = 0` returns an empty result along the selected dimension.
`maxk(A,k,dim)` selects along the specified dimension. Dimensions larger than `ndims(A)` behave like trailing singleton dimensions and return the input with index values of `1`.
`[B,I] = maxk(...)` returns selected values and one-based indices along the selected dimension.
Real, integer, logical, complex, scalar, vector, matrix, and N-D tensor inputs are supported. Integers and logical values are promoted to double precision.
Complex inputs support `'ComparisonMethod','auto'`, `'abs'`/`'magnitude'`, and `'real'`, matching the comparison options used by `max`.
GPU tensors gather to the host for top-k selection and return host tensors.

examples.description: Complex values ordered by real component

faqs.question: Does `maxk` preserve GPU residency?
faqs.answer: Not currently. RunMat gathers GPU tensors to the host because top-k provider hooks are not available yet.

faqs.question: Can `k` be zero or larger than the selected dimension?
faqs.answer: Yes. `k = 0` returns an empty result along the selected dimension. Larger values are clamped to the selected dimension length, so the full sorted slice is returned.
